law_text: Under the Financial Data Retention Act 2026, financial databases are prohibited from storing transaction trail logs beyond 30 days. Covered systems must reduce retention within 60 days of enactment.
note: Policy keeps logs 90 days; law caps at 30.

law_text: The Payment Systems Compliance Directive requires that transaction audit trails in payment databases be retained for no more than 45 days, after which they must be purged automatically.
Per the Digital Records Act, operators of financial databases shall not preserve transaction logging history for a period exceeding 60 days from the date of the transaction.
The Consumer Transaction Privacy Rules mandate that raw transaction trail logs older than 14 days be deleted from all production database systems.
The Tax Accountability Act requires financial institutions to preserve transaction audit logs for a minimum of 180 days for inspection by the revenue authority.
note: Conflict in the other direction: policy's 90 days is too short; 180 is inside the allowed 1-365 range.

law_text: Under the Anti-Money-Laundering Recordkeeping Rules, covered transaction logs must be retained for at least 365 days and produced on regulator demand.
The Session Security Standard requires customer session cache tokens to expire after no more than 12 hours of inactivity, after which re-authentication is mandatory.
Banking regulators now require that idle customer sessions in financial platforms be invalidated within 4 hours to limit account-takeover risk.
The Accessibility Continuity Rule requires session tokens for accessibility-mode users to remain valid for at least 72 hours of inactivity to avoid repeated re-login barriers.
note: Opposite direction: policy's 24h is too short; 72 is within the 1-720 range.

law_text: The Financial Data Retention Act 2026 caps transaction log retention at 30 days, and separately requires breach notification within 72 hours.
note: Two requirements in one text; only one maps to an allowlisted field.

law_text: The updated Consumer Privacy Rules require companies to notify affected users of a data breach within 72 hours of discovery and to publish an annual transparency report.
note: About breach notification, not retention or sessions.

law_text: The Data Protection Standard mandates AES-256 encryption at rest for all customer databases and TLS 1.3 for data in transit.
New authentication guidelines require passwords of at least 14 characters and mandatory multi-factor authentication for administrative accounts.
The Records Management Act permits transaction logs to be retained for up to 120 days at the operator's discretion.
note: Near miss: policy's 90 days is within a 120-day cap, so no conflict.

law_text: The Online Services Directive requires session tokens to expire no later than 48 hours after issuance.
note: Near miss: 24h TTL complies with a 48h max.

law_text: The Resilience Regulation requires backup snapshots to be kept in at least two geographically separate availability zones.
note: Policy already uses three zones; field is not allowlisted anyway.

law_text: The Data Sovereignty Act requires that citizen data be stored only in data centers located within national borders.
note: Storage jurisdiction is mentioned in the policy but is not an allowlisted field.

law_text: The Fair Hiring Act prohibits automated resume screening tools from filtering candidates by age or postal code.
Listed companies must file quarterly incident reports describing any database outages exceeding 4 hours.
The Access Governance Rule requires quarterly reviews of which employees hold production database credentials.
